To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the system for energy-aware migration of virtual machines is able to predict the future resource consumption of the VMs; 2. this prediction is based on data mining models that are able to forecast the resource consumption of the virtual machines, with an accuracy of about 90% (for the CPU consumption); 3. the system is able to save about 20% of the total energy consumption of the servers.
the proposed approach is able to reduce the energy consumption of Cloud data centres up to 30% with respect to the current state of the art.

1) the use of predictive data mining models to forecast the future resource needs of virtual machines can be effectively used to drive energy-aware migrations, and 2) the use of such models can lead to significant energy savings in Cloud servers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a data mining-based system for the efficient allocation of virtual machines on Cloud servers, in order to reduce the energy consumption of the data centre.

the following aspects: - the design of an efficient system for energy-aware migration of virtual machines; - the design and development, by means of data mining techniques, of predictive models of the future resource needs of virtual machines, in order to drive the allocation of virtual machines on the available physical servers.
the design and implementation of a system for efficient allocation of VMs, driven by predictive models.

the proposed approach can be a valid support for the Cloud provider in order to reduce the energy costs of the Cloud services, and to improve the quality of the services provided to the Cloud customers.
, the proposed system can effectively reduce the energy consumption of Cloud servers, while maintaining a high quality of service.
the proposed system is able to reduce the energy consumption of the data centres of a Cloud provider by 20%.

the system is able to reduce the power consumed by the servers by 15% on average.

we have developed a system that, based on the prediction of the resource needs of the VMs, is able to perform the VM migrations and the server consolidation in order to minimize the energy consumption of the Cloud data centre.
, the proposed system can reduce the energy consumption by 20% and 40% in comparison to the current state of the art.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of predictive models for energy-aware VM migration can lead to significant benefits in terms of power saving.
the use of predictive models for VM allocation can be a key factor to improve the effectiveness of consolidation strategies, and therefore reduce the energy consumption of Cloud data centres.
the use of data mining models for the prediction of the future computational requirements of the VMs can be used to improve the energy efficiency of the Cloud data centre.
